thread:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-serving-az15-healthcheck at 2026-03-15T02:00:34Z

ashley: saw the page, getting context. PD is repeatedly firing, looks like a flapping healthcheck upstream in az15.

jordan: I’m on-call for az15, acking now. @pagerduty acked by jordan

pagerduty: PagerDuty - Incident #INC-20260315-az15 created and acknowledged by jordan

leila: any customer impact reported yet? metrics show latency spike and 502s for a small percentage of requests to az15 only.

ashley: checking routing logs -> a subset of nodes in az15 return 502 and the autoscaler is cycling pods. Could be NIC flapping on new hardware batch.

jordan: replays of the last 15m: errors start at 02:00:10, increase at 02:00:28, PD rules retriggered twice with short gap (30s). Looks like threshold of health_check_failures=3 with window 60s is too tight for this noise.

leila: impact estimate: 2.1% of user requests, mostly via region failover we have diversion for. No customer-facing outages reported yet but SLO errors trending.

ashley: I'm going to temporarily silence the noisy PD rule for az15 and set a 5m suppression to stop repeat pages while we investigate.

jordan: +1, please add an automated note linking runbook.

ashley: done: `pd silence create --service redwood-serving-az15-healthcheck --duration 5m --note "temp suppress noisy healthcheck while investigating NIC flapping"`

sre-bot: automated action: created silence INC-20260315-az15-silence, attached runbook: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/az-healthcheck-failures

jordan: I'm spinning up a small evacuation: mark suspect nodes draining and shift new traffic to az11 and az2 for safety. Will also bump capacity in other zones to absorb the diversion.

leila: add canary routing rule to avoid model-shard-critical traffic hitting az15. We should keep embeddings and non-latency-critical traffic in az15 while routing generation requests elsewhere.

ashley: routing change in progress: `routeset update --avoid-zone az15 --traffic-type generation --percent 100` (will apply over 30s).

ops-lead: looping in hardware team; tagging oncall-az15. @oncall-az15 can you confirm if there's a scheduled maintenance or known hardware issue?

oncall-az15: no scheduled maintenance. We're seeing NIC flaps on 3 nodes in rack r-az15-12. Logs show repeated link state changes: 
```
Mar 15 02:00:09 node-az15-12 kernel: e1000e 0000:03:00.0 eth0: NIC Link is Up 10000 Mbps Full Duplex
Mar 15 02:00:11 node-az15-12 kernel: e1000e 0000:03:00.0 eth0: NIC Link is Down
Mar 15 02:00:13 node-az15-12 kernel: e1000e 0000:03:00.0 eth0: NIC Link is Up
```

oncall-az15: looks physical; hardware is flaky.

jordan: for immediate mitigation: continue draining the 3 nodes, mark them out of rotation at LB level, and trigger a node replacement (reprovision via autoscaler).

ashley: initiated drain and reprovision: `infra node replace node-az15-12-{03,04,05}`. ETA ~8m per node.

leila: can we also increase KV prefix cache TTL to reduce cross-AZ requests while traffic is diverted? small config tweak could lower load.

ashley: doing it now: `kvcache set-prefix-ttl --prefix default 300s` -> applied.

pagerduty: PagerDuty - escalation paused due to silence. No further pages will be sent for 5m.

jordan: monitoring: error rate dropping from 2.1% -> 0.4% after routeset and node drain. Still seeing occasional spikes pinned to the three problematic nodes.

ops-lead: hardware informed, RMA requested for NICs on those nodes. Hardware ETA 3 hours. We'll keep nodes replaced by reprovisioning as primary mitigation.

leila: customer comms: none needed yet, but please prepare an internal sticky note in case it escalates: impacted customers list (internal) + mitigation steps.

ashley: created incident slack thread and internal doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/INC-20260315-az15-notes. Added timeline and mitigation actions.

jordan: handoff note: I need to step out at 02:12z. ops-lead will take incident lead. jordan handing off to ops-lead.

ops-lead: acknowledged. I'm taking lead, will coordinate hardware/RMAs and confirm PD rule config change permanent if needed.

leila: next steps: let silence expire after 5m, then adjust PD rule: increase health_check_failures to 5 and window to 120s for az15 to avoid flapping pages; file follow-up to tune thresholds across newer hardware pools.

ops-lead: agreed. I will file the follow-up ticket and notify product/regional infra to tighten capacity and rolling replacement plan.

pagerduty: update: incident remains in follow-up state. No new PD notifications.

sre-bot: summary (added automatically): root cause: flaky NICs on hardware batch in az15 causing transient link flaps -> service health failures. Mitigation: silence PD, drain & reprovision 3 nodes, route generation traffic away from az15, increase kvcache TTL. Follow-up: RMA hardware, tune PD thresholds for new hardware pools, post-incident RCA.

ops-lead: closing notes: handoff to postmortem. If error rate creeps back above 0.5% for 15m, reopen channel and notify oncall. :white_check_mark:

ashley: thanks everyone, nice triage and quick mitigation.

jordan: thanks, back to rotation.

leila: adding postmortem owners: leila (ops), ashley (infra), jordan (oncall).
